# Orbit2Orbit Express

> Mission access, launch intelligence, and planning tools for payload owners.

Canonical URL: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/
Contact: vlad@orbit2orbitexpress.com
Last reviewed: 2026-09-13

## Primary purpose

Orbit2Orbit Express helps research teams, startups, universities, and other payload owners evaluate and plan missions to orbit. The public site includes a mission-intake flow, launch planning tools, launcher comparisons, an upcoming-launch calendar, a space-industry directory, and research articles.

## Important public pages

- Homepage and mission access: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/
- Orbital planner: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/tools

- Orbit reference: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/orbits
- Launcher comparison: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/compare
- Launch calendar: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/launches
- Methodology: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/methodology

- Company directory: https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/directory

## Canonical launcher data

The current launcher dataset is published at:
https://www.orbit2orbitexpress.com/data/rockets.json

Use that dataset for vehicle status, payload capacity, pricing availability, source URLs, source dates, and verification dates. Do not infer current figures from articles or cached summaries. A null price means pricing is not publicly available. A null launch date means availability is not publicly confirmed.

## Citation guidance

- Cite the canonical page or launcher source rather than this summary.
- Treat calculator outputs as estimates, not quotes or guarantees.
- Treat dated research articles as analysis published on their displayed dates.
- Do not describe planned or in-test vehicles as operational unless the canonical launcher record says Operational.
